Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 05-Jan-2026 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  FIFTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - DEC 2025 / JAN 2026  
  SUBJECT: CSE 3122/CSE_3122 SOFTWARE ENGINEERING  
  (SPL: COMPUTER SCIENCE & ENGINEERING)  
  SOFTWARE ENGINEERING [CSE 3122]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                      Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)                Identify a real-world situation where an organization can benefit from using a software product line   (5)  
  and briefly explain how it would be applied.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
1B)                Determine which Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) model is used in Automotive Software            (3)  
  Development and explain the Model with a diagram.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
1C)                Identify which Life cycle model is used in developing the Software for Safety Critical devices like    (2)  
  MRI Scanners. Explain why this model is considered to be a meta model.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2A)                Imagine a university plan to automate its course registration system, which currently depends on       (5)  
  paper forms manually entered by staff. Students need to register online, select courses, and receive  
  confirmation emails, while administrators must verify eligibility and generate timetables. As a system  
  analyst, explain how you would apply structured analysis to model this system using Data Flow  
  Diagrams (DFDs) up to Level 1, clearly identifying key processes, data stores, and data flows.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2B)                Assume a software company is developing an online examination system for a university. The draft (3)  
  SRS includes functional requirements such as user login and test scheduling but fails to specify  
  constraints on response time, concurrent users, and security measures. As requirements engineer,  
  explain how you would revise the SRS to include clear non-functional requirements, ensuring the  
  system meets both user expectations and performance standards.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2C)                Suppose a student information system has a single module responsible for attendance, fee          (2)  
  calculation, and grade entry. Identify the type of cohesion demonstrated here and suggest how you  
  would improve the module's design.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3A)                An Automatic Resume Screening System is designed to help companies automate their hiring           (5)  
  process. Recruiters can upload job descriptions and review shortlisted candidates. Job seekers can  
  
  Page #1

create profiles, upload resumes, and track their application status. The system uses AI to compare  
  candidate skills with job requirements and rank them. The admin manages user accounts,  
  recruitment analytics, and system updates.  
  Based on the above scenario, draw a Use Case Diagram showing the actors (Job Seeker,  
  Recruiter, Admin, AI Engine), use cases, and relationships (include / extend / generalization where  
  needed).  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3B)   A Smart Home Energy Management System monitors electricity usage of appliances and allows       (3)  
  homeowners to control devices remotely via a mobile app. The system also provides weekly energy  
  consumption reports and notifies users when usage exceeds limits. Draw a Level 0 DFD (Context  
  Diagram) and Level 1 DFD for this system, showing external entities, main processes, and data  
  flows and decomposition of the main process in Level 1.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3C)   Distinguish between Model-Oriented Methods and Property-Oriented Methods in formal                    (2)  
  specification, giving one example for each.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4A)   A Central Library is building an automated book checkout process. Students initiate the process by    (5)  
  scanning their Id cards at self-service Kiosk machine. Kiosk machine sends student Id number to  
  the Library Management System (LMS) to check if card is invalid or maximum books borrowed. If  
  there is any such error, LMS responds with appropriate error message. If there is no error, student  
  can further scan the book barcode. Kiosk machine sends the barcode and student Id number to  
  LMS. If the book is not reserved, LMS will reserve the book, update due date and respond with  
  appropriate confirmation message. If the book is reserved by another student, LMS responds with  
  appropriate error message. Draw a UML Sequence Diagram for the above process.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4B)   Design an activity diagram for computing a Bill in a Restaurant Management System. There should (3)  
  be a charge for each item delivered. The total amount should be subject to tax and a service charge  
  of 18% for groups of six or more. For smaller groups, there should be a blank entry for a gratuity  
  (Tip) according to the customer's discretion. Any coupons or gift certificates submitted by the  
  customer should be subtracted.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
4C)   Stock Market Monitoring System notifies multiple independent displays whenever a stock price          (2)  
  changes by Stock data object, which is not aware of specific details of Displays. Identify a Design  
  Pattern to implement one-to-many dependency between stock data and displays. Explain how this  
  pattern achieves decoupling between them.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5A)   Write a program in any programming language to check whether a given number is prime or not           (5)  
  and then perform software test coverage analysis on the code by determining the Statement  
  Coverage, Branch Coverage, and Condition Coverage.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5B)   A software company frequently updates its online banking application with new features like fund      (3)  
  scheduling and bill payments. Explain the purpose of regression testing in this scenario. Why is it  
  important to perform regression testing after every new feature addition?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  
  Page #2

5C)                   A software development team is integrating three key modules, User Authentication (A), Order      (2)  
  Processing (B), and Inventory Management (C), into a new e-commerce system. Module A is  
  complete and tested. Modules B and C have minor dependencies on A, but A does not depend on B  
  or C. Module B has critical dependencies on C to check stock before finalizing an order. The team  
  has decided to adopt an Incremental Integration Testing strategy. Given the module dependencies  
  and development status, Analyze and justify whether to use a Top-Down or Bottom-Up incremental  
  integration approach for this specific system.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  
  -----End-----
